solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Elite unit with figure like Ali M made ostentatious progress

parts.note: the SAS is the Special Air Service, the British army's elite special forces regiment
Ali M is Muhammad Ali, surname then initial; a figure like him is another boxer, David Haye, written the same way as Haye D

explanation.surface: A special forces soldier, alongside a boxing legend, strutted along in style.
explanation.walkthrough: The pattern 'Ali M' (surname plus first-name initial for Muhammad Ali) asks for another boxer in the same form: Haye D, for the British heavyweight David Haye.
explanation.definitionFit: To sashay is to walk in a showy, swaggering way, so it is moving along ostentatiously.

clue.text: President on road taken with poetic evening in port

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, US president
e'en is the poetic contraction of evening

explanation.surface: A president travels a road one evening, lines of verse in hand, towards a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen is a Scottish North Sea harbour city, a major port for the oil industry.

clue.text: Norm, maybe, in rehabilitative institution?

definitions.meaning: NORM is the first half of NORMANDY, the royal House of Normandy, so it is part of a royal house cut in two
a residence where people leaving prison or treatment readjust to ordinary life

explanation.surface: Someone called Norm is perhaps living in a rehab centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norm' looks like a man's name or a standard; it is the first half of the royal House of Normandy.
explanation.definitionFit: A halfway house is a hostel easing former prisoners or patients back into ordinary community life.

clue.text: Red Sea local with Eastern fellows in first year

indicators.note: in places the Eastern fellows inside the abbreviation for first year

parts.note: Y1, read as YI, is the abbreviation for year one, the first school year
fellows are men

explanation.surface: A native of the Red Sea coast mixes with Eastern men during the opening year.
explanation.walkthrough: Y1, year one, is written with the figure read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Yemen borders the Red Sea, so someone from there is a local of that region.

clue.text: Loss old company avoided, being skilful

indicators.note: avoided means the old company's letters are left out of the word for loss

parts.note: a deficit is a shortfall or loss
ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries, was a famous British company, now defunct

explanation.surface: A business that sidestepped losses was being cleverly managed.
explanation.definitionFit: Deft describes neat, nimble handiwork, the same thing as being adroit or skilled.

clue.text: Very clean ground on northerly route in Spanish city

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters of clean are broken up and rearranged
in a down clue, going northerly means reading upwards, so the route's letters are reversed

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, written AI

explanation.surface: A spotless journey along a road heading north ends in a Spanish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' shuffles CLEAN into ALENC; 'northerly' reverses AI (the A1, the Great North Road from London to Edinburgh) to IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Valencia is Spain's third-largest city, on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Soon to be a prolific writer

definitions.meaning: an old word for shortly or before long
..., short for anonymous, is credited with countless poems and sayings

explanation.walkthrough: The prolific author is the abbreviation used for unattributed works.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic usage gives shortly; the abbreviation for anonymous signs more texts than any named author.

clue.text: Large old English character, a king grossly discontented, showing torpor

parts.note: eth is a letter of the Old English alphabet
R stands for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: discontented means emptied of its contents, leaving only the outside letters of grossly

explanation.surface: A big, archaic figure and a hugely dissatisfied king seem utterly sluggish.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargy and torpor are both synonyms for sluggish inactivity and lack of energy.

clue.text: A fertile source in river, one subject to test?

indicators.note: in puts the source inside the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
a mine is a rich source of something, as in a mine of information

explanation.surface: A spring of fertility lies in a river, perhaps one being checked by scientists.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate sitting an exam is a person whose knowledge is being tested.

clue.text: Tight-knit group to handle broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the air, so the word sounds like the one for handle

parts.note: to handle goods is to deal in or sell them

explanation.surface: A close group is set to manage a radio or TV transmission.
explanation.definitionFit: A cell is a small unit of activists or agents working closely together within a larger body.

clue.text: Suffer financially? Help fine tech arranged

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of help fine tech are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone short of money is offered help with cheap technology.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being hard up, struggling because money is tight.

clue.text: I rate lunatic terribly lacking in fluency?

indicators.note: terribly means the letters of I rate lunatic are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone rates a madman poorly, as tongue-tied.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unable to express themselves clearly in speech is short of fluency.

clue.text: Male servers might be described as so ominous

parts.note: men are male people
tennis servers hitting unreturnable serves are acing their opponents

explanation.surface: Waiters of the male kind are described as threatening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'servers' suggests waiters; they are tennis players serving aces.
explanation.definitionFit: Menacing and ominous both describe something threatening harm.

clue.text: Thin food not half horrible left

indicators.note: not half means only one half of the word for horrible is kept, the second half dropped

parts.note: gruesome means horrible or ghastly

explanation.surface: Watery fare, partly awful, is left uneaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruel is a thin porridge of oats boiled in water or milk, the meagre fare of Oliver Twist.

clue.text: President once advancing right in depression

indicators.note: advancing means moving the letter for right further forward in the word

parts.note: Jimmy Carter was a former US president

explanation.surface: A former president gaining ground on the political right falls into a slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' suggests a mood; it is a hollow in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A crater is a bowl-shaped hollow in the ground, a physical depression.

clue.text: Crawl in Finchley

indicators.note: in means the letters lie within the word Finchley

explanation.surface: Traffic moves slowly through a London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: Finchley is a North London suburb.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch is to move slowly little by little, the way something crawls.

clue.text: One in training's disrupted after leading pair go for badges

indicators.note: in places the letter for one inside the jumbled letters
disrupted means the remaining letters are thrown into disorder
the first two letters of training's are removed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: One person's training is upset after the top pair quit, all for medals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after leading pair go' removes TR, leaving AININGS; 'disrupted' scrambles them and I goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Insignia are emblems or badges showing rank, office or membership.

clue.text: Fruit not right to go with a cheese

indicators.note: not means the letter for right is excluded from the fruit

parts.note: a gourd is a fleshy fruit of the marrow family

explanation.surface: A wrong sort of fruit is served with cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Gouda is a mild yellow Dutch cheese named after its town of origin.

clue.text: Group followed by rugby international in nerve centre

parts.note: a gang is a group of people
a Lion plays for the British and Irish Lions, the touring rugby union side

explanation.surface: A band of players tags along after a touring rugby star at headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A ganglion is a cluster of nerve cells, literally a centre where nerves meet.

clue.text: Make a mistake dropping second carrier?

indicators.note: dropping means the letter for second is lost from the word

parts.note: to stray is to err or go wrong

explanation.surface: A waiter slips up and drops another delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: A tray is a flat board used for carrying dishes or drinks.

clue.text: When retired broadcasting brothers should get insurance man

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the brothers' name is read in reverse

parts.note: Jonathan and Paul Ross are British TV and radio presenters, the Rosses

explanation.surface: When retiring, two famous brothers in media need someone to value their claims.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonathan Ross and his brother Paul are well-known British broadcasters.
explanation.definitionFit: A loss assessor evaluates insurance claims and the value of damage.

clue.text: Glittery item is largely typical of runner?

parts.note: is shortened to 's

indicators.note: largely means most but not all of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: equine means typical of a horse, a runner in a race

explanation.surface: A sparkly thing is mostly what you would expect of a racehorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' suggests an athlete; it is a horse in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequin is a small shiny disc sewn onto clothing for sparkle.

clue.text: Menu accepting yen and rupees with single starter of 'Chinese Rice for one'

indicators.note: accepting means the menu takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a menu is a list of dishes
Y is the symbol letter for yen
I, the Roman numeral one, means single

indicators.note: starter of means the first letter of Chinese

explanation.surface: A takeaway menu takes yen and rupees, plus a starter of Chinese rice for one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rice for one' reads as a solo meal; it is Tim Rice, lyricist of Evita and Jesus Christ Superstar.
explanation.definitionFit: Tim Rice is an example of a songwriter of words, writing for Andrew Lloyd Webber.

clue.text: Make good record with publishers

parts.note: rec is a short form of record
OUP is Oxford University Press, the publishers

explanation.surface: A recording deal with publishers should restore someone's fortunes.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoup is to recover losses, compensating or making them good.

clue.text: Concerned with tracing a tree?

parts.note: the tree is not botanical but a family tree, traced back through ancestors

explanation.walkthrough: 'tree' suggests a plant; it is a family tree.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective describes the study of family descent and ancestry, mapping forebears.

clue.text: Worthless van afforded covering

indicators.note: covering means the words van afforded hold the letters within them

explanation.surface: A useless van was given a cover.
explanation.walkthrough: Naff is British slang for tacky or poor quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Naff is British slang for tacky, cheap or of little value.

clue.text: Show horror close to terrifying deadly creature

indicators.note: close to means the last letter of terrifying

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: People recoil on getting near a frightening and lethal beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp intake of breath is a typical reaction of shock or alarm.

clue.text: Primate protecting small area of church

indicators.note: protecting means the primate wraps round the letter for small

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A gorilla shields a little patch of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop, fitting the church; it is a monkey-like animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the semicircular recess at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Doctor covered by popular play almost like a major criminal?

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: covered by means the doctor sits inside the other letters
almost means the play's title loses its last letter

parts.note: Faust is a play by Goethe, also Marlowe's Doctor Faustus
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor features in a hit play that is nearly a crime drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious villains are well known for wickedness, which is what the adjective means.

clue.text: Fool losing head getting to peer round moving images?

indicators.note: round means the word for peer goes around the beheaded fool

parts.note: to pry is to peer nosily

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a muppet is a fool or idiot, British slang

explanation.surface: A beheaded fool gets to snoop around films.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving images' suggests film; it is figures moved by strings or hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Puppetry makes figures move, so its images are literally animated by hand.
